findings.title: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled requires user != null, so passkeys are never offered on a fresh (unauthenticated) login
findings.body: The new helper `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` returns `webauthnAuth != null && webauthnAuth.isPasskeysEnabled() && user != null`. Both call sites that replaced the old logic (`authenticate()` line 115 and `challenge(context, error, field)` line 137) previously filled the WebAuthn conditional-UI form data when the user was NOT yet set (`context.getUser() == null`) — that is the normal first-login case where passkey autofill (conditional UI) must be offered so the user can sign in with a discoverable credential. With the new condition, `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` only runs when a user is already set in the context (re-authentication), so on a fresh login the `webauth` form / challenge attributes are never rendered and users can no longer log in with passkeys at all. This is exactly the scenario covered by the updated tests asserting `//form[@id='webauth']` is present on the initial login page, which would now fail. The condition should allow the fresh-login case (user == null) as well as the re-authentication case, e.g. by not requiring `user != null` here.

findings.title: Call to no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() does not match any declared method
findings.body: `UsernameForm.authenticate` now calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only declaration added by this PR is `protected boolean isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)` in `UsernamePasswordForm`. There is no no-arg overload in any changed file, so this does not compile. Presumably the intent was `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())` (or a passkeys-enabled check without the user requirement, since at this point `context.getUser()` is known non-null, making the `user != null` check in the helper trivially true).

findings.title: Overridden shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators missing @Override annotation
findings.body: The newly added `shouldShowWebAuthnAuthenticators(AuthenticationFlowContext)` overrides the protected method introduced in `WebAuthnAuthenticator` but lacks the `@Override` annotation, so a future signature change in the parent would silently turn this into an unused method instead of a compile error.
